items.label: 5A
items.fix: When checking sector totals against official statistics, count the allowance the filter itself grants for the gap between its total and the official figure (about 1.5%), and the published band widening, not only the copies' disagreement. The check now uses a narrower range than the model publishes, so small gaps such as hotel employment's 1.3% count as misses.
items.test: Rebuild the official-statistics page for this run; the overall share inside the range should rise from 79/100 toward 90/100, with Machinery and Oil and gas still marked as disagreeing.

items.label: 8A
items.fix: Report the headline forecast check separately for quantities the data pin down and quantities that come mostly from the model's equations (spread ratio 0.8 or above), and leave the second group out of the headline. Where nothing observes a quantity, the forecast and the later estimate come from the same equations and agree whether or not they are right.
items.test: Rebuild the forecast page; the headline should no longer include Input inventory, the model-driven New orders, Overdue and Phantom orders, and should show a lower share inside the range or a larger gap.

items.label: 1B
items.fix: Check the measure before trusting its largest values. The spread ratio averages month-by-month ratios, so a few months where the copies without data barely differ can alone produce a value like 177; a ratio of average spreads, over months that are truly uncertain, would show which sectors are really unsettled. This corrects the reading, not the filter.
items.test: Recompute the spread ratios for this run both ways; the count of ratios above 1.2 and the extreme values (177, 10.9, 8.34) should drop where they came from a few nearly certain months.

items.label: 9B
items.fix: Stop estimating per entity the observation biases that no other data can separate from the quantity they bias, such as semiconductors' lead-time bias (0% informative) and the list-price gap; hold them at their assumed values or share one value per sector. Earlier tests found that observation parameters like these barely affect accuracy, so little is lost.
items.test: Refit Semiconductors and the sectors with list prices at all four run dates; those parameters should leave the uninformative list and the forecast gaps should not rise.

items.label: 1A
items.fix: Let each kind of observation move only the quantities it measures or directly drives. Today a sector-wide statistic can nudge every quantity in the sector, including finished stock, which has no pull back toward a normal level, so accidental nudges pile up and push the copies of the world apart. Limiting finished stock to inventory observations should stop that buildup.
items.test: Filter this world's four run dates again from the existing fits with and without the change; Machinery's finished inventory (177) and Semiconductors' (8.34) spread ratios should fall below 1.2, and no other ratio should rise.

planned_by: the most likely fixes first, while the plan's expected cost stays at most $100 and its expected time under 24 hours
